transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-30 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (StratusPay Lead Eng), Carlos Mendez (Platform Eng), Janelle Park (Product)

Summary (auto): quick sync to triage two main issues seen in the pilot: intermittent function-calling failures during heavy load and structured-output JSON schema drift for the payments reconciliation flow. Discussed KV (K-V) cache warm up and autoscaling policy tweaks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Priya Desai: yep good here, thanks maya.
[00:10] Maya Chen: awesome. real quick agenda — liam will go through the benchmark we've run lightly, then we want priya to walk through the failing output examples you uploaded, then triage next steps and gating for function-calling.
[00:25] Liam O'Neill: cool, i'll share my screen, but i also posted the quick gist link in the chat, it's the p99 tail run against a small dedicated pool with our default kv-cache settings.
[00:40] Carlos Mendez: i clicked it, seeing some odd spikes around the 10 minute mark. are those synthetic or real traces?
[00:48] Liam O'Neill: those are synthetic, we replayed a 10k request workload that mirrors your peak shape — the spike aligns with cache cold starts plus a rebalancing event on the worker nodes. sometimes the autoscaler overshoots then reconverges, so you'll see a short mid-run latency blip.
[01:05] Priya Desai: is the blip because of kv cache eviction? we've seen situations where the K-V cash isn't warmed for our long-tail customers and the first invocation trips a lot of overhead.
[01:15] Liam O'Neill: yep, kv cache warm-up and prefix cache misses are the main culprit. two levers we typically suggest: 1) aggressive pre-warm (provisioned prefix population) for known keys, 2) tweak batching window slightly to allow more aggregation at p50-sensitive endpoints.
[01:30] Janelle Park: that makes sense. our primary requirement is p50 under 200ms for interactive UI flows, p99 can be up to 1s but we'd prefer lower.
[01:40] Maya Chen: good to call that out. for gating, we usually propose p50 < 250ms and p99 < 800ms as an initial check for pilot workload, then tighten in production. is that reasonable?
[01:55] Priya Desai: sounds reasonable as a staging gate. we need to be mindful of cost though — provisioning extra warm cache or larger capacity has money impacts.
[02:05] Liam O'Neill: totally — Redwood Optimize will run a quick cost delta simulation once we pick a profile. i'll include that in the benchmark output.
[02:15] Carlos Mendez: ok, second issue: structured output. we had 6% of calls failing schema validation; i attached two failing payloads earlier. priya can you talk us through those?
[02:30] Priya Desai: sure — in the reconciliation path the model returns a list of "matches" but occasionally it's returning 'match' singular or an object with unexpected keys. sometimes it also emits stray commas or a top-level string. so the JSON parser errors out and downstream processors stop.
[02:48] Maya Chen: is this using the function-calling helper in the SDK or are you parsing text output?
[02:55] Priya Desai: a mix — primary flow uses the SDK function invocation; fallback does a text-to-JSON parse. failures are coming from the fallback path when the function call times out and we try to reconstruct.
[03:10] Liam O'Neill: that aligns with what we saw. the fallback parsers are brittle when the model is in a degraded mode or when the prompt gets very long. two mitigations: enforce stricter function signatures with required fields so the runtime rejects weird shapes, and add a simple shim on your side to coerce single objects into arrays when appropriate.
[03:30] Janelle Park: the problem is sometimes it's not coercible, there's context missing. we need to capture the exact prompt/response pair for investigation.
[03:38] Priya Desai: i'll upload the three representative failing prompt/response pairs we saw yesterday.
[03:44] Maya Chen: perfect — that will help liam reproduce. liam, are you able to run a replay with the exact traces?
[03:50] Liam O'Neill: yes, if priya uploads them to the shared drive i'll run them through our sandbox runtime and toggle the function-call timeout and the structured-output parser settings. i'll add the results to the ticket.
[04:05] Carlos Mendez: about the function-call timeout — currently we're using a 1.5s client timeout. i guess that's borderline?
[04:12] Liam O'Neill: 1.5s is tight for some heavier workflows. with dedicated capacity and warmed cache we usually see p50 ~120-180ms on our medium models, but spiky sequences with long KV lookups can push >500ms. increasing to 2.5s or adding a soft-deadline with early partial responses is another option.
[04:30] Priya Desai: what's the impact on token cost if we increase the timeout or change batching?
[04:36] Liam O'Neill: timeout alone doesn't change tokens; batching window increases tokens-per-batch but reduces CPU/GPU overhead per token so cost/unit tends to drop. there is a tradeoff with tail latency — more batching can increase p50 slightly but reduce p99 dedicated cost. we'll give you the delta numbers in the benchmark artifact.
[04:55] Janelle Park: can you also show us the quantization/precision profile you used in the dedicated pool? some of our legal folks ask about fp16 vs int8 artifacts and how that interacts with hallucination rates.
[05:10] Liam O'Neill: we used an int8-ish profile for the load test to be cost realistic, but we can re-run with a higher-precision profile. quick note: hallucination rates depend more on prompt engineering and evaluation harnesses than quantization for these models, but we'll include a short regression check.
[05:30] Maya Chen: switching gears, priya — you mentioned two failing structured-out JSON examples. can you paste the raw one now?
[05:38] Priya Desai: sure, here — response 1 shows an array but with mixed types: [ {"id": "abc123"}, "unexpected_string", {"id": "xyz"} ] — our validator fails.
[05:50] Liam O'Neill: thanks, that's a pretty clear parse mismatch. i'll try a stricter function signature and force the SDK to only accept top-level arrays of objects.
[05:58] Carlos Mendez: and what's the SDK behavior when the function returns non-JSON? does it surface the raw text?
[06:04] Liam O'Neill: yes, the SDK surfaces both the raw model text and the parsed payload if available. in your fallback path it's the raw text, so your parser is the last line. we recommend using the SDK's validate-and-normalize helper which will attempt coercions and return structured error objects.
[06:20] Priya Desai: we didn't realize that helper existed, that might simplify our integration.
[06:24] Maya Chen: we'll send a short code snippet highlighting the helper and suggested error handling patterns after the call.
[06:30] Janelle Park: great. question on security — our security team wants to confirm KMS key rotation and that Redwood does not see plaintext of customer-managed keys. status?
[06:40] Maya Chen: short answer: for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS and Redwood's control plane does not have access to your CMK private key material. for Hosted/Dedicated we provide envelope encryption patterns with customer-managed keys in supported cloud KMS providers — i'll attach our security whitepaper and SOC 2 addendum.
[07:00] Carlos Mendez: ok please attach that. also we need the VPC peering checklist — we hit a networking snag last week where the peering was set up but traffic restricted by an ACL.
[07:10] Maya Chen: will do. we'll add a short checklist and common ACL rules to the runbook.
[07:18] Priya Desai: back to performance — can you explain the autoscaler overshoot you mentioned earlier? is it the default kubernetes-based policy?
[07:26] Liam O'Neill: it's a custom autoscaler — it favors quick scale-ups to keep tail latency low, sometimes overshooting when there's a short-lived spike. tuning the cooldown window from 60s to 120-180s helped in other customers with similar bursty traffic. also tying scale triggers to application-level metrics (cache miss rate) instead of just cpu helps.
[07:48] Janelle Park: any risk to consistency or dropped requests when you extend cooldown?
[07:53] Liam O'Neill: minimal if you have a small burst buffer and prefix cache prewarm. the idea is to let a small transient spike be absorbed without spinning up many instances that later idle.
[08:05] Maya Chen: quick note — we also ran a canary with the function-call soft-fallback enabled which returns a structured partial result and a continuation token when the model can't complete. this reduced hard failures by ~40% in internal tests.
[08:20] Priya Desai: that continuation token idea could work — we could retry with a narrower prompt or hand off to a simpler heuristic process.
[08:28] Carlos Mendez: about telemetry — are you able to surface per-request input prompt size and token breakdown in the console? our ops team wants to correlate prompt length with failures.
[08:36] Liam O'Neill: yes, the console traces include token counts, per-token latency, and a kv-cache hit/miss tag if you enable the prefix-caching telemetry. we'll show you the fields in the dashboard export.
[08:48] Maya Chen: shall we pivot to timeline and gating: what needs to be green to move to next phase?
[08:55] Janelle Park: from product side: structured-output pass rate > 99% on smoke tests, p50 < 250ms for core flows, and documented mitigation for the remaining edge cases.
[09:05] Priya Desai: engineering wants reproducible benchmarks that match our traces and a plan for private key handling if we go Private.
[09:12] Maya Chen: ok so immediate items: 1) liam runs replay benchmarks, 2) priya uploads traces and failing payloads, 3) maya sends runbook + security attachments. any other blockers?
[09:24] Priya Desai: maybe one more — we saw an intermittent 502 from the SDK layer when a worker restarted. can you explain the retry semantics?
[09:32] Liam O'Neill: the SDK has exponential backoff with jitter by default for transient 5xx; it will retry up to 3 times with increasing delay. in your case we also saw a failing healthcheck that caused the worker to drain, which coincided with the 502. increasing graceful shutdown time on your side helped in one test.
[09:50] Carlos Mendez: ok we'll look at graceful shutdown.
[09:55] Janelle Park: question for sales — any change to pricing if we pivot to dedicated pool earlier?
[10:02] Maya Chen: pricing tiers for Dedicated are committed monthly capacity; we can discuss a short-term trial commit to prove performance with a billing credit offset — i'll follow up with a formal quote after the benchmark.
[10:15] Priya Desai: are there limits on model variants we can pin for dedicated? we wanted to try two small/medium variants side-by-side.
[10:22] Liam O'Neill: yes you can pin model families and we support multi-variant routing. that is part of the Dedicated configuration and we'll include suggested profiles in the benchmark report.
[10:33] Maya Chen: ok we're approaching the last 20 minutes — liam do you want to walk through a quick demo of the sandbox replay UI?
[10:40] Liam O'Neill: sure, small demo — i'll show the trace upload, the toggle for KV prewarm, and how we change the function-call timeout per route.
[10:48] [screen share noise] Liam O'Neill: here you can see the uploaded trace, we toggle prewarm and re-run; notice the p50 drops by ~70ms after prewarm.
[11:05] Priya Desai: curious — how do you determine which keys to prewarm? we have thousands of customer keys and can't prewarm all.
[11:12] Liam O'Neill: good question — we recommend a hot-key heuristic: prewarm keys that appear in the top 5% of traffic or those tied to SLAed flows. we also support an LRU-style warm window and targeted prewarm APIs.
[11:26] Carlos Mendez: could you share the script you used to generate the synthetic 10k workload so we can reproduce locally?
[11:33] Liam O'Neill: yeah i'll add it to the artifact bundle. it's in the gist link.
[11:38] Janelle Park: ok last item — can we agree on tentative dates for the deep-dive after the benchmark?
[11:45] Maya Chen: propose 2026-10-12 or 2026-10-13 for a 60–90 minute deep dive with your infra + security. which works?
[11:52] Priya Desai: 10/12 works for us.
[11:55] Maya Chen: great. i'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[12:00] [wrap-up silence]
[12:05] Maya Chen: recap — liam runs the full benchmark and posts results and cost delta by 10/07. priya uploads traces and two failing examples by 10/04. maya sends security runbook and VPC checklist by 10/01. deep-dive set for 10/12. anything else?
[12:20] Carlos Mendez: nope that's it from me. thanks all.
[12:25] Janelle Park: thanks, bye.
[12:30] Priya Desai: thanks, bye.

Notes about transcription: occasional word swaps (K-V cash instead of KV cache), timestamps approximate, some speaker labels simplified. Links referenced: gist://redwood/benchmarks/stratuspay-20260930, drive://stratuspay/trace-uploads, security://redwood/soc2-addendum.pdf
